Quality checks on a fit's published quantities

Source: R/quality.R
mfbdfm_quality.Rd

Measures the mixing and the precision of what is actually published, which parameter diagnostics do not. Meant as a gate: if a check fails, keep the last publication and investigate, rather than lowering the bar.

Usage

mfbdfm_quality(
  fit,
  exact = NULL,
  unexplained = NULL,
  ess_min = 400,
  mcse_max = 0.1,
  rhat_max = 1.01,
  anchor_max = 0.001,
  fallback_max = 0.01,
  param_ess_min = 100,
  exact_z = 3,
  unexplained_max = 0.5
)

# S3 method for class 'mfbdfm_quality'
print(x, ...)

Arguments

fit

A fitted model carrying its draws, the default.

exact

Optional result of mfbdfm_exact() on fit.

unexplained

Optional single number: the published revision minus the sum of its news, in annualised points.

ess_min, mcse_max, rhat_max, anchor_max, fallback_max, param_ess_min, exact_z, unexplained_max

The limits, see Details.

x

An object from mfbdfm_quality().

...

Ignored.

Value

A data frame of class "mfbdfm_quality" with columns check, value, limit, pass. A check that does not apply here is left out. pass is NA for one that cannot be judged, such as a constant chain. The attribute pass is TRUE only if no row has pass of FALSE.

Details

For the latest unobserved nowcast (annualised percentage points), and for an ind_dfm() fit also for the latest weekly factor value and the mean of the latest 13 weeks:

ess

Rank-normalised effective sample size, at least ess_min.

mcse

Monte Carlo error of the mean, sd / sqrt(ess), at most mcse_max.

rhat

Split R-hat from one chain cut in half, at most rhat_max.

And for the fit as a whole:

anchor

An ind_dfm() nowcast reproduces the observed target, largest absolute difference at most anchor_max.

rho_fallback

How often rho was forced to rho_fallback rather than drawn, at most fallback_max of the draws per series. An ind_dfm() fit.

parameters

The smallest effective sample size among the identified parameters, at least param_ess_min.

exact

With exact, the chain's latest nowcast differs from mfbdfm_exact()'s by at most exact_z joint Monte Carlo errors.

unexplained

With unexplained, the part of a revision the news decomposition leaves unexplained is at most unexplained_max.

The default limits follow Vehtari et al. (2021) for ESS and R-hat. The limit on the Monte Carlo error is a judgement about one-decimal communication: mcse_max of 0.10 means that two runs differ by about 0.14 (one standard deviation).

References

Vehtari, A., Gelman, A., Simpson, D., Carpenter, B., & Burkner, P.-C. (2021). Rank-normalization, folding, and localization: An improved R-hat for assessing convergence of MCMC. Bayesian Analysis, 16(2), 667-718. doi:10.1214/20-BA1221

See also

mfbdfm_diagnostics() for every parameter, mfbdfm_exact().

Other model functions: mfbdfm_contributions(), mfbdfm_diagnostics(), mfbdfm_draws, mfbdfm_exact(), mfbdfm_news()

Examples

# \donttest{
data(mfbdfm_example_data)
set.seed(1)
fit <- ind_dfm(mfbdfm_example_data, length_sample = 200, burn_in = 50)
